the_run.reserve: authored from the traced arm on the CUT board and thinned to the stations at least 0.60 mm from every detour's own fixed terminal -- 14 discs of r 0.30 mm on B.Cu, exempt BQ25185_SYS

why_it_failed_exactly.1_rebond_priced: the spec's eighth object is a BARREL -- ILIM_VSET 0.600/0.300 at (69.25,76.45) -- and it ties that net's In3.Cu stub to its B.Cu run.  A barrel is always `relay: false`, `--repair-planes` only stitches POUR-OWNING nets, and ILIM_VSET owns no pour, so the In3.Cu stub (0.9192 mm at 68.6,77.1) and the B.Cu stub (0.2121 mm at 69.4,76.6) are left dangling and the net regresses.  In3.Cu is a RESERVED plane (+3V3, D-580), so the ONLY lever that can put that stub back is `--detour-own-layer` (D-609)
why_it_failed_exactly.2_the_lane_cannot_be_authored: 32 of the 78 arm stations inside this pocket are within 0.60 mm of one of the detours' OWN FIXED TERMINALS -- the closest is 0.258 mm -- so a disc that reserves those stations seals the copper it displaced (D-667).  The 14 discs that CAN be placed do not bound the arm, and the relaid detours take it back: `pour_partition` false, no net improved.  This is D-663's *'freeing a pour is a null transaction unless the lane is reserved'* meeting D-667's *'the reservation is stronger than the rule it stands for'* at the same pocket
